qc/runs/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r2/manifest.json (seed hashes), raw-evidence-index.json (head; no seed-specific runtime evidence)
evidence: Shipped data files: environment/assets/seed_data.json and solution/app/src/seed_data.json are byte-identical (28549 bytes, sha256 a1c65c80...7f83740, matching manifest.json lines 9 and 24); the only other shipped JSON is solution/app/package.json. No CSV/TSV. Seed parses as JSON (Python json.load). Scripted integrity check (run locally, read-only, in Python over the frozen file) found zero defects: 10 users, 3 jobs, 16 applications, 127 messages, 3 notes, 6 read markers; unique ids and unique user emails; stages list equals candidate_status_labels keys and matches hireops_rules.md section 7 wording exactly; every job's recruiter_id is a recruiter and manager_id a hiring_manager; interview_limit in 1..50 (3/2/3); every application job_id resolves; all candidate emails well-formed and unique per job case-insensitively (Noor Haddad is on JOB-PLAT and JOB-DSGN, allowed by rules section 2); positions are contiguous 1..n within every (job, stage); Interview occupancy 2/3, 1/2, 1/3 never exceeds the limit; the single REJECTED card APP-301 has rejected_from=SCREEN and a non-blank reject_reason, and no non-rejected card carries reject fields; candidate account names match their application candidate_name. Messages: every application_id and sender_id resolves; every sender is permitted to write in that conversation under rules section 6 (recruiters, the job's own manager, or the owning candidate; no observer messages); no blank bodies; uniform keys; timestamps sorted per thread; APP-101 has exactly 120 messages tagged (#001)..(#120) consecutively, supporting app_context.md:30 ('120 messages at the start') and the 30/page paging criteria (functional judge.toml:317, :326; 120 = 4 pages). Notes: application/author ids resolve; authors are a recruiter or that job's hiring manager (MGR1 on JOB-PLAT, MGR3 on JOB-DSGN). Read markers: all ids resolve; candidates only hold markers on their own applications; 1 <= read_count <= thread length, no duplicate (user, app) pairs; the golden maps read_count to message ids at db.js:82-83, which is safe since every count >= 1. Seed-dependent grader fact checked: Lena (USR-CAN3) marker 2 of 3 on APP-301, message #3 sent by USR-REC3 -> 1 unread, matching functional prompt.md:25 and judge.toml:335 ('Lena Fischer starts with 1 unread'). Clean/synthetic: all email domains are reserved .example (hireops.example, candidates.example, mail.example); names are generic synthetic; no phone numbers, addresses, DOBs, URLs, non-ASCII oddities; regex scan for HTML/script tags, template expressions, SQL fragments, prompt-injection phrases ('ignore previous', 'system prompt'), and password/secret/token/api-key strings matched nothing except ISO timestamps (false hits on a digit pattern). No credential lives in the seed: users carry no password field; the shared demo password Hireops!2026 appears only in the brief/rules/app_context and the golden's seeding code (db.js:63), which the skill profile and the Internal sheet annotation treat as expected. generated_note is a benign provenance sentence. Adversarial attempts: (a) broken app that ignores read markers would show Lena 0 unread and is caught by judge.toml:335; a naive 'total - read_count' unread computation would mis-count own messages but rules section 6 explicitly says own messages are never unread, so that is a fair, public trap rather than a seed defect. (b) Conforming alternative: an app that, per 'sending a message counts as having read', normalises read markers up to a user's own last message yields identical observable unread and seen states for every seeded thread (computed: REC3/APP-301 unread 0 either way and CAN3's #2 still seen; CAN1/APP-101 unread 0 either way and REC1's #119 still seen), so no conforming reading is penalised by the data. Notes (not defects): (1) two markers sit below the holder's own last message (USR-CAN1 on APP-101 read_count 119 while CAN1 sent #120; USR-REC3 on APP-301 read_count 2 while REC3 sent #3), a state not reachable through the product's 'sending counts as read' rule but without observable consequence under the public rules; (2) narrative nit: APP-301 is rejected yet the recruiter's last message (2026-07-29) promises a follow-up after the panel; cosmetic only, candidate sees 'Not moving forward'. Runtime: no runtime evidence specific to seed loading was required for this row; the scripted golden run indexed in raw-evidence-index.json binds the same seed hash but is not a configured judge run.
